summary: Gille and Parimala prove a local-global principle for twisted flag varieties over a semiglobal field F = K(X), K the fraction field of a complete DVR with arbitrary residue field k: if the characteristic exponent p of k does not divide the order of the automorphism group of the absolute root system of G_ad, a twisted flag of G has an F-point if it has points over all completions at divisorial valuations of normal models, and only valuations nontrivial on K are needed (Theorem 5.4). Without the condition on p, the same holds with all points of the special fibre of one model, with all rank-one valuations, or when G extends to a reductive model (Theorem 4.5, Corollaries 4.6–4.8). The proof combines an analytic factorization of elementary and R-trivial subgroups over a patching diamond (§3), field patching (§4), and tame loop torsors after a prime-to-p finite structure reduction (§5), with a purity theorem for torsors on regular surfaces (§7). 152 items (7 library, 4 planned, 141 missing) are routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations (SF.0, SF.1, SF.2, SF.4), ReductiveGroupsPartII (RG2.0, RG2.0a), InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups (IG.0, IG.1), DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra (R03.3) and the proposed ReductiveGroupsPartIISemiglobalFlags. Nineteen findings are recorded: the Tits-index formulas print the inclusion reversed, the purity theorem omits codimension-zero points, three proofs have gaps with repairs, two corrections are already in Gille's errata (whose witness series is itself wrong), and one finding concerns HHKP20. Independent review: retain partial status until the explicit supplier gaps and dependency closure are completed. General type/parabolic/form interfaces remain imports of the upstream ReductiveGroups roadmap.

items.name: Smooth connected restriction over finite algebras
items.statement: If A is a nonzero finite k-algebra and H is reductive over A, Res_A/k H is a smooth connected affine k-group. It need not be reductive.
items.note: Requires the nilpotent-algebra and inseparable Weil-restriction smoothness/connectedness results, beyond the separable reductivity clause of RG2.0a.

items.note: Supply the comparison of endpoint-unit localizations; a bare point bijection is not sufficient.

items.name: R-equivalence insensitive to the Artin nilpotents
items.statement: For the same A=product A_i and H, H(A)/R ≅ product_i H(k_i)/R.

items.name: Square-zero devissage of finite local algebras
items.statement: For local Artin A with maximal ideal m and m^(n+1)=0, use A_j=A/m^(j+1), j=0,…,n. The kernel A_j→A_(j−1) is m^j/m^(j+1), square-zero for j≥1.
items.note: API: Finite tower and Lie-valued congruence kernels of smooth groups. Tests: (1) A=k[epsilon]/epsilon³ has two nontrivial steps; (2) At j=2 the kernel is m²/m³, not mA_j; (3) The tower ends at A_n=A, not A_(n−1). The manuscript writes m_j = m^j/m^(j+1) = mA_j; the second equality is a slip (E1).

items.name: Vector-kernel torsors preserve R-classes in the nilpotent tower
items.statement: In the finite-Artin smooth-group tower the Weil-restricted kernel is a vector group Lie(H) tensor the square-zero ideal; its torsor over the affine previous stage is trivial, giving a scheme product and an isomorphism on R-classes.
items.note: Use vanishing of H1 of quasi-coherent additive sheaves on affine schemes, not the false assertion that every unipotent torsor is trivial.

items.name: Elementary subgroup equals R-trivial subgroup over fields
items.statement: For a semisimple simply connected strictly isotropic group over a field, H(k)^+=RH(k).
items.note: This is not the assertion H(k)^+=H(k); Kneser–Tits vanishing is stronger.

items.name: Elementary subgroup equals R-trivial subgroup over finite algebras
items.statement: For semisimple simply connected strictly isotropic H over a finite nonzero k-algebra A, H(A)^+=RH(A); reduction and restriction of scalars identify the elementary and R-equivalence quotients with the product over residue fields.
items.note: Use henselian invariance and the preceding field theorem, retaining semisimplicity.

items.statement: Under the module data V is closed in R0, and likewise W.

items.name: Norm on localized module elements
items.statement: If v=u/t^n with u in V but not tV, then |v|=alpha^n; zero is handled separately.

items.name: Module as the integral ball in its localization
items.statement: V={v in V[1/t]: |v|≤1}; this is open and closed in V[1/t].
items.note: The author text prints |v|≥0, which is all of V[1/t]. The integral-ball inequality is ≤1. (E2)

items.name: Localized modules are Banach subspaces
items.statement: V[1/t] and W[1/t] are closed K-vector subspaces of F0 and hence complete for the restricted norm.
items.note: These spaces need not be finite-dimensional over K.

items.name: Analytic functions have a strict derivative
items.statement: For normed spaces over a nontrivially normed field, an analytic function at x has strict derivative fderiv at x; in this application all spaces are complete.
items.note: Read Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Analytic.lean:141–145 at 082e2d3; apply with the complete spaces here, and restrict scalars and precompose with closed-subspace inclusions. The manuscript states strict differentiability with one fixed constant β (E4); the true notion, which this library result supplies, has the remainder o(|x2 − x1|).

items.name: Strict submersion maps a neighbourhood filter onto a neighbourhood filter
items.statement: For complete normed spaces E,F over a nontrivially normed field, if f has strict derivative f′ at a and range(f′)=top, then map f (nhds a)=nhds(f(a)).
items.note: Read Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/FDeriv.lean:76–98. No complemented kernel or finite-dimensional K-space hypothesis is required.

items.name: Corrected local analytic surjectivity
items.statement: For the module data, let f be analytic on an open neighbourhood of (0,0) in F0^a×F0^b, f(0,0)=0, a,b,c>0. If Df_v(V[1/t]^a)+Df_w(W[1/t]^b)=F0^c, some epsilon>0 has every y with |y|≤epsilon in f((V^a×W^b)∩domain(f)).
items.note: Apply the library strict submersion theorem to the restricted K-Banach domain. The second module must be W; the manuscript also mis-types one derivative domain. This item is a proved correction proposed for review, not a silent quotation. (E3; the literal printed statement was the checkpoint's item 37, now recorded only as E3.)

items.name: Analytic multiplication-type factorization near zero
items.statement: For equal input/output dimension n and analytic f with f(x,0)=f(0,x)=x near zero, the module hypotheses imply that all sufficiently small y are f(v,w) with v in V^n and w in W^n.
items.note: Both partial derivatives are identity, so the corrected derivative condition follows from V+W=R0.

items.name: Optional closure factorization theorem
items.statement: If E/F is separable, H/E semisimple simply connected, and G_F0 strictly isotropic, then closure(RG(F1))=RG(F1)RG(F2)=G(F0)^+.
items.note: Statement read from the page image; the closure bars are essential. Not used by Theorem 3.13 or later. The printed proof has misprints in Claim 3.12 (E7) and asserts normality without proof (E8); the repair uses items 57, 125, 149, 150 and 151. items.name: Open subdirect product repair in the optional theorem
items.statement: For H open in a finite product of the relevant elementary simple-factor groups, if each projection is onto, H∩G_i is open and normal in G_i. If every proper normal subgroup of G_i is central and an open subgroup cannot be central, then H is the whole product.
items.note: Surjective projections alone do not make H normal: the diagonal of S3×S3 is a counterexample. H∩G_i is normalized by H, hence by p_i(H) = G_i, and it is open; an open subgroup of the nondiscrete group G_i(F0)^+ is not contained in its finite centre, so Tits' theorem (item 150) gives H∩G_i = G_i. This repairs E8.

If a smooth F-variety Z has points over F_v for every nontrivial rank-one valuation v with T contained in O_v, there is a regular projective T-model whose every closed-fibre point P (including generic points) has Z(F_P) nonempty, with F_P=Frac(completed O_model,P).

No separability of F/K is assumed in HHKP; GP26's smooth geometrically integral curve gives a narrower application. Do not replace all rank-one T-valuations by only discrete ones. Completion is maximal-ideal completion, not just t-adic completion at a closed point.

items.name: Purity for reductive torsors on a regular surface
items.statement: For a regular noetherian scheme X of dimension at most two, an open U containing every point of codimension at most one, and reductive G/X, restriction H1_fppf(X,G)→H1_fppf(U,G) is bijective. In the integral dimension-two case this is CTS79 Theorem 6.13.
items.locator: Author Theorem 7.1(i); published Theorem B.1(i); CTS79 Theorem 6.13, pp. 128–129

Proof uses vector-bundle extension, a locally chosen affine linear quotient for an isotrivial reductive group (CTS Corollary 6.12), twisting, and unique gluing via affine Isom schemes. Main integral-model application is unchanged. (E17)

items.name: Purity with an affine linear quotient
items.statement: Let X be regular noetherian of dimension at most two and j:U⊂X contain all codimension-zero and codimension-one points. Let G be affine and Zariski-locally admit a closed immersion G→GL_n such that the fppf SHEAF quotient GL_n/G is represented by an affine X-scheme. Restriction of fppf G-torsors from X to U is an equivalence of groupoids, hence induces a bijection on H1_fppf.
items.locator: Author Theorem 7.1(ii); published Theorem B.1(ii); CTS79 Lemmas 2.1–2.2, Theorem 6.13 proof and Remark 6.15
items.note: G4 discharged with an explicit correction to GP26's stated open-subset scope, not by attributing that correction to the authors. Items 130–137 give the proof. Affine Hartogs extends a quotient section; the represented fppf sheaf quotient makes GL_n→GL_n/G an epimorphism with torsor identity. No independent flatness assumption on G is used in this sheaf-level argument, and no flatness of the quotient map is claimed. A merely affine categorical quotient is insufficient. The local constructions glue by unique extension of affine Isom torsors. Item 138 tests the missing codimension-zero condition. (E17)

items.note: The main application is contained in corrected item 90. CTS proof inspection is complete for this step: induce a GL_n-torsor, extend its vector bundle, extend the affine quotient section and pull back the universal H-torsor; full faithfulness gives uniqueness and Zariski gluing. Do not impose the field-valued torsor arguments on an arbitrary categorical quotient.

A loop cocycle takes values in G(B), not all G(B_n); a loop torsor is a torsor class represented by one.

items.name: Tame covers are dominated by Kummer-unramified covers
items.statement: For regular henselian A and a divisor cut by coordinate parameters, a tame finite etale cover of U is dominated by a cover obtained from a finite etale A-algebra and prime-to-p roots of the parameters, by Abhyankar’s lemma.
items.note: Use the correctly inverted Kummer algebra on U. The phrase finite degree prime to p alone is not a sufficient criterion for tame Galois closure. Independently checked source correction recorded as E22.

items.name: Prime-to-p finite-group torsors are loop torsors
items.statement: If S/A is finite etale of constant degree prime to p, every S-torsor over U is a loop torsor, and its image under S→H is a loop H-torsor.
items.locator: Gille 2024 Lemma 3(2),(3), cited as Lemma 2.3 in GP26
items.note: Read pp. 162–163. For tameness, first make S constant by an unramified cover; inertia then has image in a group of order prime to p. This supplies the needed justification beyond the printed connected-cover degree argument. Independently checked source correction recorded as E21.

items.name: Completion comparison for the local and completed local rings
items.statement: For the regular two-dimensional local ring R_P and A=its maximal-ideal completion, their Grothendieck-valuation completions of fraction fields agree under the natural embedding: they have the same uniformizer and residue field k(P)(u), and successive approximation is dense.
items.note: The equality is between complete valued fields. Merely sharing residue and uniformizer would not identify arbitrary noncomplete subfields. This is the justification in Gille's errata (E16).

items.name: Smooth proper fixed locus for a tame geometric loop action
items.statement: For a loop cocycle acting on a smooth proper A-scheme Z, twist by the arithmetic part and take the fixed locus of its finite prime-to-p diagonalizable geometric part. The resulting Y is smooth proper over A.
items.note: Use the linearly reductive/tame fixed-locus theorem; no wild fixed-locus smoothness is asserted.

items.name: Fixed-point criterion over the Grothendieck completion
items.statement: For henselian regular local A with full coordinate divisor, affine finitely presented G acting on smooth proper Z and a loop cocycle phi, the twisted Z has a point over the Grothendieck completion iff its arithmetic-twisted geometric fixed locus has a k-point iff the twisted Z has a U-point.
items.note: Proof specializes the proper point through the tame extension and successive Laurent coordinates, then uses smooth henselian lifting. Extra divisor coordinates may be inverted for the GP26 fraction-field application.

items.name: Parabolic criterion for loop reductive groups
items.statement: For a loop reductive U-group and a star-stable type I, a U-parabolic of type I exists iff the geometric loop action normalizes such a parabolic over the residue field of the arithmetic twist iff the group over the Grothendieck completion has such a parabolic.
items.locator: Gille 2024 Theorem 6 (cited as Theorem 4.1(iii)⇒(i) in GP26)
items.note: Directly read the published prerequisite pp. 164–165; its numbering differs from the cited preprint. This is the descent input, not ordinary henselian lifting alone.

items.name: Divisorial points yield a model with completed-local points
items.statement: Under the main prime-to-root-automorphism-order hypothesis, if a twisted flag has points at every divisorial completion, there exists a regular proper T-model on which it has an F_P-point for every special-fibre point P.
items.note: Use finite structure reduction, SNC spreading, the corrected completed local A, the common Grothendieck completion and the loop parabolic criterion. Generic points are already divisorial.

items.name: Divisorial local-global principle for twisted flags
items.statement: Let F=K(X) be semiglobal as specified and p the characteristic exponent of k. For reductive G/F assume p does not divide |Aut(Phi(G_ad,F_s))|. Every twisted flag Z of G satisfies Z(F)≠empty iff Z(F_v)≠empty for every discrete valuation arising from codimension-one points of normal projective T-models.
items.note: Combines Proposition 5.2 with Corollary 4.6. The residue field is arbitrary; do not add finiteness/perfection or rationality of G.

items.name: Only valuations nontrivial on the constant field are needed
items.statement: In the main divisorial theorem, it suffices to test divisorial valuations v whose restriction to K is nontrivial.
items.note: This is a restriction of the tested family, not an extra hypothesis on every discrete valuation of F.

items.name: Replacement of the root-system order hypothesis by finite reduction
items.statement: The proof works whenever the type-preserving form torsor reduces to a finite F-subgroup of degree prime to p with the integral finite-etale/spreading control needed by the proof.
items.note: Keep the finite-subgroup reduction as actual supplied data; avoid asserting every reductive form admits a prime-to-p reduction.

items.name: Type G2 residue-characteristic refinement
items.statement: For type G2 the main divisorial local-global conclusion holds if the residue characteristic is not 2, using a finite structure reduction of 2-primary degree.
items.note: Source assertion: p=3 is allowed in this refinement although 3 divides the root-system automorphism order. The finite reduction requires its own prerequisite proof.

items.statement: For reductive G/F, an algebraic subgroup P is parabolic when P is smooth and G/P is projective. Projectivity of the quotient alone is insufficient in positive characteristic.
items.note: API: Parabolic predicate, quotient representability and extension of scalars. Tests: (1) G itself is an allowed parabolic; (2) A Borel of split G is parabolic; (3) Do not accept a non-smooth Wenzel subgroup solely from projective quotient.

items.name: A parabolic quotient is transitively acted on over every extension
items.statement: If P⊂G is parabolic, then for every field extension E/F the action G(E) on (G/P)(E) is transitive.
items.note: Borel–Tits conjugacy for rational parabolics; this is stronger than geometric transitivity.

items.name: Universal field-point transitivity gives a rational section
items.statement: For an algebraic subgroup P with projective quotient G/P, if G(E) acts transitively on (G/P)(E) for every E/F, then G→G/P has a rational section.
items.note: Apply the condition to E=F(G/P) and the generic point, using the base coset as the other point.

items.name: A rational section forces smooth connected stabilizer
items.statement: For reductive G/F and P with projective quotient, a rational section of G→G/P implies P is smooth connected.
items.note: After algebraic closure set Q=(P_red)^0; Q is smooth and parabolic, G/Q→G/P is finite with a rational section, hence finite birational onto the normal target and is an isomorphism.

items.name: Smooth stabilizer is exactly parabolic in a projective quotient
items.statement: For P⊂G with G/P projective, P smooth connected implies P smooth, and P smooth implies P parabolic. These complete the five-way equivalence of Proposition 6.1.
items.note: Separate the substantive smoothness implication above from these definition-level implications.

items.name: Twisted flags are universally transitive
items.statement: A twisted flag X of G has transitive G(E)-action on X(E) for every extension E/F.
items.note: Transitivity on an empty X(E) is interpreted as the pairwise property; it does not assert an E-point.

items.name: Universal transitivity characterizes twisted flags
items.statement: Let X be a nonempty integral smooth projective G-variety. If G(E) acts transitively on X(E) for every extension E/F, then X is a twisted flag of G.
items.note: Over F_s choose a smooth point, identify the orbit quotient by its stabilizer, then apply Proposition 6.1. Retain the standing variety convention to exclude the empty scheme.

items.name: Orbit-stabilizer scheme identification
items.statement: Under the universal transitivity hypothesis over a separably closed field and a chosen rational point, the orbit map identifies G/P with the smooth projective variety, with P the scheme-theoretic stabilizer.
items.note: Pointwise geometric transitivity alone cannot erase infinitesimal stabilizer information.

items.name: Finite birational morphism to a normal target is an isomorphism
items.statement: A finite birational morphism from an integral scheme to a normal integral scheme is an isomorphism; apply to G/Q→G/P after the rational section supplies equality of function fields.
items.note: Include finiteness and normality; a general proper birational map need not be an isomorphism.

items.name: Vector groups are R-trivial and additive torsors vanish on affines
items.statement: Affine-space points are directly R-equivalent by linear interpolation, and H1 of a quasi-coherent additive sheaf on an affine scheme is zero; together these justify the vector-torsor step in Lemma 2.3.

items.name: Etale maps remain etale after finite locally free restriction
items.statement: Whenever the relevant Weil restrictions are representable, restriction along a finite locally free base map preserves etale morphisms, including a finite inseparable field extension.

items.name: Etale charts are local analytic isomorphisms over the complete valued field
items.statement: At a rational point of an etale morphism of smooth finite-type F0-schemes, the induced map on F0-points admits a local analytic inverse.
items.note: Bridge the scheme etale Jacobian criterion to the normed analytic inverse function theorem; no finite residue assumption.

items.name: Smooth points lift from the residue field of a henselian local ring
items.statement: For henselian local A and smooth finitely presented X/A, X(A)→X(k) is surjective.
items.note: This geometric statement is beyond a bare ring Hensel predicate; the complete local ring used in Proposition 5.2 supplies the hypothesis.

items.name: Central isogenies and adjoint quotients preserve parabolic schemes
items.statement: The parabolic schemes, types and associated twisted flags of a reductive group are identified with those of its adjoint quotient and of the simply connected cover of its derived group.
items.note: Transport group actions through the central morphisms without claiming surjectivity on all rational group points. Independent review: import this general structure/classification interface from the named upstream layers. The semiglobal continuation only assembles its use; it must not construct a second general parabolic/type/form theory.

items.name: A power subgroup of torus points is R-trivial
items.statement: For a torus T over a field, a suitable positive integer n has T(L)^n⊂RT(L) for the relevant extensions, via a quasi-trivial torus resolution and an isogeny lifting the power map.
items.note: The exponent is essential. This does not assert T(L)=RT(L). The approximation application remains part of G2. Used in Claim 3.12 (E7).

items.name: Elementary points are dense under the patch-field embedding
items.statement: In the strictly isotropic setting, polynomial coordinates on the unipotent radicals and density F1⊂F0 make G(F1)^+ dense in G(F0)^+ in the comparison needed for Proposition 3.6.
items.note: Prove this for finite products of root/unipotent words and their closures; density of the full G(F1) alone does not imply density of an arbitrary subgroup.

items.name: Finite algebras are Artinian with nilpotent nilradical
items.statement: A module-finite algebra over an Artinian ring is an Artinian ring; the nilradical of a commutative Artinian ring is nilpotent.
items.note: Read Artinian/Module.lean:403 and Artinian/Ring.lean:63. Use these existing results for the finite-algebra tower, not a new Artinian theory.

items.name: Artinian quotient decomposition
items.statement: For commutative Artinian R and n, R/(nilradical R)^n is canonically isomorphic as an R-algebra to the product over maximal ideals m of R/m^n.
items.note: Read Artinian/Module.lean:625. Together with nilradical nilpotence this supplies the product algebra; the finite-local-algebra item only asks for the residue-factor and torsor comparison packaging.

items.name: Reflexive modules via the existing dual evaluation
items.statement: Use Module.IsReflexive R M: the canonical evaluation M→Dual R (Dual R M) is bijective. This is the module notion used stalkwise for the coherent extension argument; it is not derived or topological reflexivity.
items.note: API: Import Module.IsReflexive, bijective_dual_eval and evalEquiv from Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Defs.lean (read at the pinned commit); do not create a second predicate. Tests: (1) A finite free module over a field is reflexive; (2) Z/nZ for n>1 is not reflexive as a Z-module since its dual is zero; (3) For M=0 evaluation is the unique equivalence, so the zero case must be retained in freeness statements.

items.name: Hartogs for finite locally free sheaves
items.statement: If X is noetherian and U contains every point x with depth O_X,x at most one, then a finite locally free sheaf E on X is canonically j_*(E|U). In particular O_X=j_*O_U and sections extend uniquely.
items.note: Use the local-depth criterion for extension across the complement. On a regular surface, codimension equals local dimension and depth, so the codimension-at-most-one condition suffices. Tau Ceti Scheme/Regular.lean only supplies a dimension-at-most-one Hartogs interface, not this missing surface statement.

items.name: Hartogs extension of affine scheme sections
items.statement: If O_X→j_*O_U is an isomorphism for an open immersion j, then for any affine X-scheme Y the restriction Y(X)→Y(U) is bijective.
items.locator: CTS79 Lemma 2.1(iii), p. 109; explicit generalization of its finite-type version
items.note: Write Y=Spec_X(A). Sections are algebra maps A→O_X. Adjunction identifies maps A→j_*O_U with maps j*A→O_U. No finite-presentation assumption on A is needed for this argument. This is the affine-only extension step, not an assertion for all separated or proper targets.

items.name: Coherence of the extension of a vector bundle
items.statement: For noetherian X and U containing all points of depth at most one, a finite locally free E on U has coherent direct image j_*E.
items.note: Work locally on X; extend E's dual to a coherent sheaf, take a finite presentation, dualize to embed E into O_U^r, and extend using j_*O_U=O_X. The resulting subsheaf of a coherent finite free sheaf is coherent. Retain noetherian and quasi-compactness hypotheses.

items.name: Reflexivity of the coherent Hartogs extension
items.statement: With the preceding hypotheses, j_*E is reflexive. If X is regular, its stalks at points of codimension at most two are free.
items.note: Identify double-dual evaluation on U, then extend using the dual presentation and Hartogs. The stalkwise freeness conclusion imports item 134 from the commutative-algebra owner; do not define a new derived reflexivity notion.

items.name: Reflexive finite modules over small-dimensional regular local rings are free
items.statement: For a regular noetherian local ring R of Krull dimension at most two and a finite reflexive R-module M, M is finite free, including M=0.
items.locator: CTS79 Lemma 2.2 proof, p. 110; local algebra used by Theorem 6.13
items.note: R03.3 already plans finite global dimension for regular local rings and Auslander–Buchsbaum. Add only this corollary: a reflexive module is a second syzygy from a finite dual presentation, hence has depth at least min(2,dim R); finite projective dimension and Auslander–Buchsbaum give pd=0, and finite projective modules over a local ring are free. Handle M=0 separately. No completeness, coefficient DVR or arithmetic deformation data are needed.

items.name: Vector bundles extend across codimension two on a regular surface
items.statement: For regular noetherian X of dimension at most two and U containing all codimension-at-most-one points, finite locally free sheaves on X and U are equivalent by restriction, with inverse j_* on such sheaves.
items.note: Coherence, reflexivity and item 134 give local freeness at every point; Hartogs for Hom bundles gives full faithfulness. Translate through the frame-bundle equivalence to obtain GL_n-torsor extension. Variable rank is locally constant; use a fixed n on each trivializing open. These are SF.0 exports, not consumers of SF.1 purity.

items.name: Full faithfulness of affine torsor restriction
items.statement: Under O_X=j_*O_U, restriction on fppf torsors under an affine X-group G is fully faithful.
items.locator: CTS79 Theorem 6.13 uniqueness and twisting argument; affine Hartogs proof
items.note: Isom_G(P,Q) is represented by an affine X-scheme: fppf-locally it is G and affineness descends. Item 131 extends an isomorphism uniquely; its inverse extends too and identities hold by uniqueness. This proof does not assume G flat or finite type independently of the fppf torsor condition.

items.statement: Given a G-torsor P on U under the hypotheses of item 90, extend E_U=P×^G GL_n to a GL_n-torsor E on X via item 135. Its reduction section of E_U/G extends to E/G, which is affine by descent. Pull back the universal G-torsor E→E/G along the section; glue the locally constructed extensions with item 136.
items.locator: CTS79 Theorem 6.13, p. 129; Remark 6.15, p. 130; GP26 Appendix B.1(ii)
items.note: API: Induction of torsors, associated quotient E×^GL_n(GL_n/G), reduction/section equivalence, restriction comparison and unique descent. Tests: (1) G=GL_n returns vector-bundle extension; (2) A trivial torsor's identity reduction extends to the trivial torsor; (3) The proof accepts a represented fppf sheaf quotient, but does not accept an arbitrary affine categorical quotient lacking the epimorphism and torsor identity.

X is regular noetherian of dimension two and U contains every codimension-one point, but restriction on PGL_2-torsors is not injective: choose the same trivial torsor on A²_R and respectively the split matrix algebra and Hamilton quaternion algebra on Spec R.

items.name: Smooth rank-one completion points descend to the henselization
items.statement: For a rank-one valued field L and a smooth finite-type L-variety Z, Z(L_v) nonempty implies Z(L_v^h) nonempty.
items.note: Use an étale chart about a smooth completion point and the henselian implicit function argument with density of L. The rank-one completion is henselian. Route the general valued-point result to RG2.0; do not impose discrete valuation or finite residue field, and do not drop smoothness.

items.name: An infinite compatible quadratic-transform chain gives a valuation ring
items.statement: Let X_i be regular projective T-models successively blown up at finite sets of closed points, and choose compatible points P_i in those centers. The directed union O=colim O_X_i,P_i is a nontrivial valuation ring of F containing T.
items.note: For each f∈F×, Lipman 1969 Theorem 26.2 says the points cannot all remain indeterminacy points for f, so some local ring contains f or f^−1. Local transition maps keep t in the maximal ideal, making the valuation nontrivial. This uses two-dimensional point blow-ups, not arbitrary-dimensional resolution.

items.name: Henselization and fraction fields along the quadratic-transform chain
items.statement: In item 144, O^h≅colim O_X_i,P_i^h compatibly over O, and Frac(O^h) embeds in colim F_P_i.
items.note: Filtered colimits of local henselian rings are henselian; the colimit is ind-étale over O and has the same residue field as O. The residue field is the colimit of the stage residue fields, not necessarily equal to every stage field (avoid that shortcut in the printed proof). Compatible embeddings of the henselizations into completed local rings give the last inclusion. Import the existing henselization/local-ring carrier owner rather than recreate it. The printed shortcut is recorded as E19, a finding in the cited source.

items.name: Only finitely many model points can remain bad
items.statement: For smooth Z/F with points over all rank-one T-valued completions and any regular projective T-model, the set of closed-fibre P with Z(F_P) empty is finite and consists of closed points.
items.locator: HHKP20 Theorem 2.5 first paragraph, p. 7; HHK15 Proposition 5.8
items.note: At each generic point η there is a rank-one completion point. Spread to a nonempty affine open U in that irreducible component avoiding the others, using HHK completed-patch spreading. Inclusions F_U⊂F_P give points for P∈U; the remaining points on finitely many proper curves form a finite set. HHK's proof interior remains in the ledger.

items.name: Termination of blowing up the bad-point set
items.statement: Under item 83's hypotheses, repeatedly blowing up all bad closed points eventually produces a model without bad points.
items.note: If all bad sets stay nonempty, finite branching gives a compatible infinite path. Item 144 gives v∈Ω_F of rank one or two; rank-one smooth descent plus item 142 in rank two gives a point over Frac(O^h). Item 145 and finite presentation descend that point to some F_P_i, contradicting badness. Finite-stage descent must be proved; do not assume that arbitrary functors commute with filtered colimits.

items.name: The rank-one T-valuation family already tests twisted flags
items.statement: In the GP26 semiglobal setting, for any reductive G/F and twisted flag variety Z/F, Z(F) is nonempty iff Z(F_v) is nonempty for every v∈Ω_F^1.
items.locator: HHKP20 Theorem 2.5 combined with GP26 Corollary 4.6(1); explicit strengthened consequence
items.note: A smooth flag variety meets HHKP's hypothesis; obtain a model with points at every F_P and apply GP26's model-point local-global theorem. This uses a subset of all rank-one valuations, strengthens the wording of author Corollary 4.8(1), and is recorded as a deduction rather than a quotation. No prime-to-root-automorphism order condition enters this argument. Independent review: the model-point local-global input is GP26 Corollary 4.6(1); Corollary 4.7 is the different reductive-model/discrete-valuation result.

items.name: Prasad's form of Tits' theorem on open subgroups
items.statement: Let k be a field henselian for a nontrivial non-archimedean valuation, and G a semisimple almost k-simple group. Then every proper open subgroup of G(k)^+ is bounded; equivalently, an unbounded open subgroup of G(k)^+ equals G(k)^+.
items.locator: Proposition 3.11(2) proof, p. 14, citing [K-P, Proposition 2.14]; Prasad, Bull. SMF 110 (1982), Theorem (T)
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. Read in Prasad 1982, pp. 198–201: the only field hypothesis is that k is henselian for a nontrivial non-archimedean valuation, so it applies to the complete discretely valued F0 with an arbitrary residue field. This settles the scope question of the checkpoint's gap G2. Kaletha–Prasad, the reference GP26 cites, was not read.

items.name: Tits' normal subgroup theorem
items.statement: Let k be a field with at least four elements and G a simply connected, almost k-simple, k-isotropic semisimple group. Every subgroup of G(k) normalized by G(k)^+ is central or contains G(k)^+; in particular every normal subgroup of G(k)^+ is central or all of G(k)^+.
items.locator: Proposition 3.11(2) proof, p. 15 ('Tits' theorem'); Tits, Annals of Math. 80 (1964), main theorem
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. GP26 names the theorem without a reference; the statement is the standard one and Tits 1964 was not reread here. The repair of E8 (item 57) uses it for each factor G_i.

items.name: Approximation of a maximal torus from a dense subfield
items.statement: Let F1 ⊂ F0 be a dense subfield of a complete valued field, G a reductive F1-group and T a maximal F0-torus of G_F0. Then there is a maximal F1-torus T♯ of G such that T♯_F0 is G(F0)-conjugate to T (by an element close to 1).
items.locator: Claim 3.12 proof, p. 14, citing [Hd, proof of Hauptlemma]
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. Proof: the variety of maximal tori is rational, so its F1-points are dense in its F0-points, and the orbit map of G on it is smooth, so G(F0)-orbits are open. GP26 says T♯_F0 is 'isomorphic to T'; the argument needs conjugacy (E7). Harder 1968 was not read.

items.name: Gluing a torsor to its generic extension
items.statement: Let X be an integral noetherian scheme with function field F and H an affine flat X-group scheme of finite presentation. Let V1, V2 ⊂ X be open and P_i an H-torsor on V_i, with P_1 and P_2 isomorphic over F. Then the isomorphism extends over a nonempty open W ⊂ V1 ∩ V2, and P_1 and P_2 glue to an H-torsor on V1′ ∪ V2, where V1′ = V1 minus the closure of (V1 ∩ V2) \ W.
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. The isomorphism spreads out by finite presentation of the affine Isom scheme, and V1′ ∩ V2 ⊂ W. Gille–Pianzola 2008 was not read; this is the gluing the proof of Lemma 5.1 uses.

items.name: Finite flat group schemes are linear with affine quotient
items.statement: A finite flat group scheme S over Z (more generally over a Dedekind ring) admits a closed embedding S ⊂ GL_N, and the fppf quotient GL_N/S is represented by an affine scheme.
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. This puts S0 in the scope of Lemma 5.1 and of purity (item 90). Neither source was reread here.

items.name: Reductive groups on a regular surface are locally linear with affine quotient
items.statement: Let X be a regular noetherian scheme of dimension at most two and G a reductive X-group scheme. Zariski-locally on X there is a closed embedding G ⊂ GL_n with GL_n/G represented by an affine scheme; hence case (i) of Theorem 7.1 is a special case of (ii).
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. The checkpoint read CTS79 Corollary 6.12, which supplies the local linear embedding with affine quotient used in the proof of item 89.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: semiglobal flags and R-equivalence
routes.brief:
Build Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: semiglobal flags and R-equivalence. Import Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), especially Layers 2–9, instead of re-planning its group, root, parabolic, central-cover and Chevalley constructions. Import affine Weil restriction and generalized valued-point charts from Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0a, RG2.0), geometry/descent/lifting from Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0–SF.4), and tame covers from Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0–IG.1). Keep these producers independent of this consumer. Existing Mathlib strict submersion and analytic differentiation supply the Banach analysis; do not rebuild them or assume finite dimension over K.

Import the parent’s general parabolic representability, anisotropic type, form/diagram torsor and central-isogeny flag interfaces (items 5, 7, 12, 124). Construct their type-preserving reduction and semiglobal applications; semilocal R-equivalence and elementary subgroups with nilpotent-Artin invariance; the product-compatible last unipotent subgroup and its Lie spanning chart; corrected analytic factorization on saturated complete T-modules V,W; restriction of projective flags along arbitrary finite, possibly inseparable, extensions. Prove Theorem 3.13 for the specified diamond with F1 dense in F0 and F1 intersect F2=F, using the supplied module hypotheses. Give separate elementary and R-factorization statements with each isotropy hypothesis retained. Optional Proposition 3.11 is not used by Theorem 3.13; build it with the repaired proof (Prasad's Theorem (T), Tits' normal subgroup theorem, torus approximation, and the open-factor argument of item 57), and keep it out of the main dependency chain.

Build the normal-model point/open/branch fields and finite patching system, including the finite P1-model map and tensor decompositions. Prove Z(F) nonempty iff all finite-patch points exist for every reductive G/F and twisted flag Z, and deduce the all-special-fibre-points and unconditional all-rank-one-valuations forms. Read HHKP20's precise family Omega_F of nontrivial valuations whose rings contain T; testing its rank-one subfamily already suffices. Prove the finite bad-point set, blow-up termination, rank-two coarsening and finite-stage point descent, importing SF.4's valuation-limit/henselization interface and RG2.0's smooth completion-to-henselization theorem. With a reductive model, prove the discrete-valuations form without a residue-characteristic restriction. State the Tits-index corollaries using Delta_0 equal to minimal-parabolic type: the global subset is the smallest Gamma_F-stable subset containing the transported local subsets. This is the correction recorded as E13; the manuscript prints the inclusions reversed.

For the final theorem let T be any complete DVR, K its fraction field, k its arbitrary residue field, F=K(X) for a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and p the characteristic exponent of k. If p does not divide the order of the automorphism group of the absolute root system of G_ad, prove Z(F) nonempty iff Z has points over all divisorial completions of F arising from normal projective T-models. It suffices to test those nontrivial on K. Import SF.0–SF.1's corrected affine-quotient surface purity, whose local freeness step imports DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3; do not omit codimension-zero points or replace the represented fppf quotient by a categorical quotient. Prove the finite-subgroup reduction, SNC spreading, prime-to-p finite-etale loop reduction and loop-parabolic criterion; complete the local ring at P before applying henselian arguments and prove the Grothendieck-completion comparison. The G2 refinement requires residue characteristic different from 2 and its special finite-reduction proof. Do not replace the divisorial family by a fixed model or omit the order hypothesis.

Every definition/construction has an API and three tests in the items. Mandatory boundary tests include nonreduced E tensor F_i, a proper but not strictly proper parabolic in a product, a non-smooth projective quotient in characteristic p, the factorial-pole series outside Frac(k[x][[t]]), and the corrected V/W derivative condition. The tests of finite algebra and Tits-index conventions must import the existing carriers. Prove, rather than encode as structure fields, every external theorem contract. Before implementation, extract the exact prerequisite proof interiors listed in the ledger. Suggested future files may separate REquivalence, AnalyticFactorization, PatchFields and TwistedFlags; this paper job supplies no Lean file and asserts no formalization.
routes.reason: The parent owns algebraic groups and general relative structure, while the existing RG2 continuation concerns local fields with finite residue field, buildings and parahorics. Neither owns semilocal R-equivalence, semiglobal patching or tame-loop flag descent. FunctionFieldArithmetic concerns global finite-constant-field arithmetic and is not this owner. sourceIssues.reason: Take T=k[[t]], u=x^(-1), F1=Frac(k[[u,t]]) and R0=k((u))[[t]]. The finite sums s_N=sum_(n=1)^N t^n u^(-n!) lie in F1∩R0 and form a t-adic Cauchy sequence. Its R0-limit s is not in F1: otherwise b s=a with nonzero a,b∈k[[u,t]]. Divide their common lowest t-power so b_0(u)≠0 and put d=ord_u b_0. In the t^n coefficient of b s, b_0 u^(-n!) has order d−n!, while every other term b_j u^(-(n−j)!) has order at least −(n−1)!. For n!−d>(n−1)!, the unique lowest-order term cannot cancel, contrary to a having no negative u-powers. Thus F1∩R0 is not complete. The correction uses exactly the complete modules already proved in Lemma 4.3 and leaves the theorem intact.

sourceIssues.reason: Prime-to-p degree alone does not imply tameness of a connected cover. In characteristic 2 take A=F2[[s,t]], U=Spec A[1/(st)], and the monic cubic X^3+sX+t. It is irreducible over Frac(A): a monic factorization over the integrally closed A would specialize at s=0 to a factorization of the Eisenstein polynomial X^3+t. Its discriminant is t^2, so it defines a connected finite etale cover of U of degree 3. At the t-divisor the quadratic residue factor X^2+s gives a purely inseparable residue extension of F2((s)), so the cover is not tame. The missing justification is supplied by the finite-group torsor hypothesis, as already outlined in item 99; the lemma itself survives.
